name: VLT UT1 / KMOS

MAN.document: ESO, KMOS User Manual, Doc. No. ESO-264148, Issue 6.1.1, 2024-07-04 (J. M. Corral-Santana on behalf of the KMOS IOT; the current ESO Period 115 manual). Page numbers are the manual's own page labels (PDF page = label + 7)

DEV.document: ESO "K-band Multi-Object Spectrograph - KMOS" development-projects page (the consortium baseline specification; retrieved 2026-11-18)

M10.document: Sharples, R., et al. 2010, The Messenger 139, 24, "Recent Progress on the KMOS Multi-object Integral Field Spectrometer" (ADS 2010Msngr.139...24S; title checked on ADS). Open access; 4 pages (journal pp. 24-27). Final-design values; Table 3 gives the filter bandpasses and the design resolution

M13.document: Sharples, R., et al. 2013, The Messenger 151, 21, "First Light for the KMOS Multi-Object Integral-Field Spectrometer" (ADS 2013Msngr.151...21S; title checked on ADS). Open access; 3 pages. Commissioning narrative only: it holds no optical prescription (read in full; it is cited for the first-light date)

S07.document: Sharples, R., Ramsay Howat, S., Davies, R. & Lehnert, M. 2008, "KMOS: Design Overview and Calibration Requirements", 2007 ESO Instrument Calibration Workshop (ADS 2008eic..work..311S; title checked on ADS). 7 pages, preliminary-design-phase text; holds the only open optical raytrace figure (Fig. 3, PDF p. 6) and the 256 mm slit

D13.document: Davies, R. I., et al. 2013, A&A 558, A56, "The Software Package for Astronomical Reductions with KMOS: SPARK" (ADS 2013A&A...558A..56D; arXiv:1308.6679; title checked on ADS)

D10.document: Davies, R., et al. 2010, Proc. SPIE 7735, 77356V, "KMOS data flow: reconstructing data cubes in one step" (ADS 2010SPIE.7735E..6VD; arXiv:1005.4748; title checked on ADS)

S14.document: Sharples, R. & the KMOS Team 2015, IAU Symposium 309, 11, "KMOS @ the VLT: Commissioning and Early Science" (ADS 2015IAUS..309...11S; title checked on ADS; Cambridge open-access PDF, 6 pages, journal pp. 11-16)

VLT.document: ESO, "Requirements for VLT UT Instruments", VLT-SPE-ESO-10000-2723, Issue 1 (18.03.2005), Table 3 "Nasmyth focus optical parameters" (copy of the file saved for UVES, round 5)

parameters.quote: Entrance pupil diameter 8000 mm
parameters.note: as the MUSE and UVES presets: D = 8.0 m. KMOS is on UT1 (Antu): S14 Sec. 2.1 "Nasmyth focus of the VLT UT1 telescope"

parameters.value: f/15; 582 um/arcsec
parameters.quote: Focal ratio 15.000 ... Image scale slightly field dependent 582
parameters.note: DERIVED: one 0.2 arcsec spaxel is 0.2 x 582 = 116 um in the telescope focal plane; the KMOS pickoffs and IFU fore-optics re-image it (the explorer does not model them)

parameters.quote: The patrol field of the pick-offs is 7.2 arcmin in diameter, which is the diameter of the un-vignetted field at the VLT Nasmyth focus
parameters.note: VLT: unvignetted 7.15 arcmin (VLT Table 3)

parameters.value: 24 arms, in two layers of 12
parameters.quote: The pick-off arms are arranged into two different planes ("top" and "bottom") of twelve arms each
parameters.note: each arm: fold mirror at the tip, lens collimating the beam and re-imaging the pupil on a cold stop in the arm, roof mirror (path compensation), fold, K-mirror assembly (MAN Sec. 2.2.2, p. 7)

parameters.value: vacuum-spaced doublet, flat telecentric focal plane
parameters.quote: below a vacuum-spaced doublet corrector which produces a flat telecentric focal plane
Each IFU has a square field of view of 2.8 × 2.8 arcsec

parameters.value: 14 slices of 0.2 arcsec x 2.8 arcsec, 14 spaxels per slice
parameters.quote: partition each sub-field into 14 identical slices, with 14 spatial pixels along each slice
parameters.note: D13 Sec. 6: "the slitlets are 0.2′′ × 2.8′′" (quote checked in the Notes)

parameters.quote: ensures uniform spatial sampling of 0.2x0.2 arcsec

parameters.parameter: Slice width on the sky = the slit (explorer slitW)
parameters.note: DERIVED: the sampling is 0.2 x 0.2 arcsec and the field is 14 slices x 0.2 arcsec = 2.8 arcsec; the slice width is the dispersion-direction slit width, 0.2 arcsec = 2 detector pixels (see the FWHM line below)

parameters.quote: reimage it with 2:1 anamorphic magnification onto the image slicers
parameters.note: Same trap as MUSE: the isotropic explorer reads the along-slit scale at about half the real 0.2 arcsec per spaxel

parameters.value: 3 re-imaging mirrors; slicer mirror array of 14 spherical slices; two pupil mirror arrays of 7 facets; slit mirror array of 14 toroidal facets
parameters.quote: one monolithic slicing mirror array containing 14 slices with spherical surfaces in different orientations; two monolithic pupil mirror arrays containing seven facets ... one monolithic slit mirror array containing 14 facets with toroidal surface form

parameters.parameter: Pseudo-slit length at the spectrograph entrance
parameters.quote: reformatted into a single 254-mm long slit at the entrance to the three spectrometers
parameters.note: CONFLICT: S07 (2007 design text) gives 256 mm (quote below)

parameters.value: 256 (112 slices from 8 subfields)
parameters.quote: Each IFU sub-module produces a 256mm long slit containing 112 separate slices from 8 subfields.

parameters.value: 112 slitlets (8 IFUs x 14 slices); 1568 spaxel spectra
parameters.quote: of 336 dispersed slitlets across the 3 detectors
parameters.note: DERIVED: 336 / 3 = 112 slitlets per detector; 112 x 14 spaxels = 1568 = 8 x 14 x 14. This is the explorer's nObj (KCWI 3330 and MUSE 3600 count spaxels the same way)

parameters.quote: the mean distance between left or right edges within any IFU is always almost exactly 18 pixels
parameters.note: DERIVED: 14 slitlets x 18 px = 252 px (4.54 mm) per IFU; 8 IFUs = 2016 px of the 2048

parameters.parameter: Slitlet width on the detector (along the slit)
parameters.quote: The mean slitwidth is 13.6 pixels
parameters.note: DERIVED: 14 spaxels in 13.6 px = 0.97 px per spaxel, so the true scale along the slit is 0.2 / 0.971 = 0.206 arcsec per px. D10 abstract: "each about 2000 pixels in the spectral direction and 14 pixels wide spatially"

parameters.value: along pixel columns (vertical in the pipeline figures)
parameters.quote: with the spectral axis approximately aligned with pixel columns on the detectors
parameters.note: the explorer's Nx is the dispersion axis: 2048 either way

DERIVED: 2048 px x 18 um = 36.864 mm of chip for the 254 mm slit gives 0.1451; per IFU 252 px x 18 um = 4.536 mm over 254 / 8 = 31.75 mm gives 0.1429 (the 256 mm slit gives 0.144 and 0.142). Taken as 0.1451. This is f_cam / f_col of the isotropic spectrograph

parameters.parameter: Slice width on the slit mirror
parameters.note: DERIVED: 2 px x 18 um = 36 um on the chip / 0.1451 = 0.248 mm; sky scale at the slit 0.2 arcsec / 0.248 mm = 0.806 arcsec per mm (effective focal ratio of the beam into the spectrograph: see EFFECTIVE F below)

parameters.quote: The measured FWHM of the spectral lines is 2 pixels
parameters.note: S14/OVR: "Nyquist sampling (~2 pixel) of the spectral resolution element at the detector"

parameters.value: < 1 px (0.2 arcsec) across the slices; about 1.3 px (0.25 arcsec) along the slices
parameters.quote: shows a FWHM of < 1 pixel (0.2 arcsec) in the direction across the slices and ≈1.3 pixels (0.25 arcsec) in the spatial direction within the slices
parameters.note: the manual's own pixel-to-arcsecond ratios are not consistent with 2 px per 0.2 arcsec across the slices (see Conflicts)

parameters.value: telecentric, F/16 along the slit and F/44.7 in the spectral direction
parameters.quote: The input beam from the IFU is telecentric with an f-ratio of F/16 in the slit direction and F/44.7 in the spectral direction due to the anamorphic magnification of the IFU fore-optics.
parameters.note: the spectral (dispersion) direction sets R, so the explorer's single F is 44.7

parameters.value: flat, about 30 x 400 mm, between the slit and the collimator; folds the axis parallel to the Nasmyth flange
parameters.quote: The fold mirror is a flat optical element of approximately 30mm ... 400mm in size

parameters.value: single toroidal mirror, about 50 x 330 mm, tilted at 4.5 deg to the incoming beam
parameters.quote: The collimator mirror is a single toroidal optical element of approximately 50mm ... 330mm in size and tilted at 4.5º to the incoming beam.
parameters.note: tilt convention: see Notes (the explorer's colTilt = 4.5 deg, the mirror's tilt, not the 9 deg deflection); the figure shows the returned beam 8.6 deg off the incoming one (MEASURED, Fig. 1)

parameters.quote: The collimator focal length is 1000mm.

parameters.note: DERIVED: f_col / F_spectral = 1000 / 44.7 = 22.37 mm at the collimator (along the slit 1000 / 16 = 62.5 mm). The paper gives no beam diameter. The grating's clear aperture, 120 mm along the ruled dimension and 60 mm across (T06 Sec. 2.2), is larger than the beam

parameters.value: reflective monolithic ruled (or replicated) grating, operated in order -2, oriented almost normal to the camera
parameters.quote: The grating is a reflective monolithic ruled (or replicated) type operated in the –2nd order orientated almost normal to the spectrograph camera.
parameters.note: as built (MAN Sec. 5.1): 2nd order for IZ, YJ, H, K and first order for HK

parameters.parameter: Grating angle and groove density, range
parameters.value: angle to the incident beam about 30 to 47 deg; groove density about 200 to 500 lines/mm (no per-band table)
parameters.quote: The angle with respect to the incident beam varies between approximately 30º and 47º, the groove density varies between approximately 200 and 500 lines/mm.
parameters.note: the paper has NO per-band table: the per-band densities below are FITTED to the manual's dispersions and are tested against these ranges

parameters.value: clear aperture about 120 mm along the ruled dimension x 60 mm across; designed for I/z, J, H, K and the combined I/z&J, J&H, H&K bands, six on the wheel
parameters.quote: The clear aperture of each grating is approximately 120mm along the ruled dimension and 60mm across. The optical design includes gratings for the individual I/z, J, H, and K atmospheric bands, as well as for the three combined bands I/z&J, J&H, and H&K.
parameters.note: the beam (22 to 33 mm along the dispersion) does not fill the ruled length: gLen is not needed

parameters.value: the grating angle de-magnifies the slit image in the dispersion direction; with the IFU's 2:1 the total is 2:1 (Nyquist)
parameters.quote: This grating angle leads to an anamorphic de-magnification in the dispersion direction, which together with the anamorphic magnification of the IFU fore-optics results in a total anamorphic magnification in the dispersion direction of 2:1
parameters.note: the explorer computes this factor itself from the grating geometry

parameters.value: six spherical lenses of four IR materials: CaF2, E-SF03, CaF2, E-SF03, fused silica, ZnSe
parameters.quote: The spectrograph camera consists of six lenses made from four different infrared materials
parameters.note: lens order: "The first and third lens are made from Calcium Fluoride, the second and fourth from the Hikari glass E-SF03, the fifth lens is made from fused silica, and the last lens from Zinc Selenide." (M10: "six-element transmissive achromatic camera")

parameters.value: 145 mm; F/4.6 in the spectral direction, F/2.3 in the spatial direction
parameters.quote: The spectrograph camera focal length is 145mm and has an f-ratio of F/4.6 in the spectral direction and F/2.3 in the spatial direction.
parameters.note: DERIVED: f_cam / f_col = 145 / 1000 = 0.145, against 36.864 mm of chip / 254 mm of slit = 0.1451 (independent check)

parameters.quote: It is oriented at a fixed angle of 32º to the collimated beam.
parameters.note: MEASURED from Fig. 1: 33 deg between the incoming collimated beam and the camera axis (grating to the detector focus)

parameters.parameter: Slit image width, before the grating
parameters.quote: we convolved a top-hat input slit corresponding to 2.8 pixels width with the diffraction PSF of the spectrograph in spectral direction
parameters.note: DERIVED check: slice on the slit 0.2 arcsec x 8000 mm x 44.7 = 0.347 mm; x 0.145 = 50.3 um = 2.79 px of 18 um; the grating's de-magnification (cos alpha / cos beta, 0.68 to 0.86) brings it to about 2 px

parameters.value: slit curvature about 1 mm (60 of 2048 px); spectral distortion 0.09 to 0.25 mm at the slit ends
parameters.quote: the effect is rather small (60 out of 2048 pixels) and will be included in the wavelength calibration

parameters.value: R exceeding 3200 over z, J, H, K (Fig. 3 plots R and the exit-slit width against wavelength; the plot is a figure, not read)
parameters.quote: Nyquist sampled spectra in the wavelength range covering the atmospheric bands z, J, H, and K with a resolving power exceeding 3200

parameters.value: single off-axis toroidal mirror (reflective)
parameters.quote: Each spectrograph uses a single off-axis toroidal mirror to collimate the incoming light
parameters.note: ALT (INST, Spectrographs): "Each spectrograph uses a single off-axis toroidal mirror to collimate the incoming light, which is then dispersed via a reflection grating and refocused using a 6-element transmitting camera." ON-/OFF-AXIS VERDICT: OFF-AXIS (stated in every source). T06 gives the tilt (next rows); do NOT set colTilt 0

parameters.value: reflection gratings, one 5-position wheel per spectrograph
parameters.quote: The five available gratings (IZ, YJ, H, K, HK) are mounted on a 5-position wheel
parameters.note: CONFLICT: S14 Sec. 2.4 and T06 Sec. 4.1 say a six-position wheel; MAN and INST say five (the manual adds a blank position for calibrations)

parameters.value: second order for IZ, YJ, H, K; first order for HK
parameters.quote: By design, KMOS gratings IZ, YJ, H and K work in 2nd order.
parameters.note: HK: "... grating works already in first order" (p. 37, in the list of ghost properties)

parameters.value: Teledyne substrate-removed HAWAII-2RG HgCdTe, 2048 x 2048, 18 um pixels, one per spectrograph
parameters.quote: Detector type Substrate removed Hawaii 2RG ... Number of pixels 2048 x 2048 ... Pixel size 18
parameters.note: operating temperature 35 K (MAN Table 2); the optical bench is at 115-120 K (S14 Sec. 2.1; INST)

parameters.value: three-axis translation stage (focus; flexure compensation)
parameters.quote: mounted on a three-axis translation stage

parameters.value: order-sorting band-pass filters in the filter wheel ahead of the IFU fore-optics
parameters.quote: Immediately in front of the fore-optics is a filter wheel, which is used for order-sorting with the selected gratings.
parameters.note: bandpasses in the table below (M10 Table 3)

parameters.value: one cryostat, three identical modules (8 arms + 8 IFUs + 1 spectrograph + 1 detector each)
parameters.quote: KMOS was designed to have three identical modules, each of them comprising eight pickoff arm systems, eight d-IFUs, one spectrograph and one near-IR detector.
parameters.note: the three spectrographs are in a plane perpendicular to the Nasmyth rotation axis (S07 Sec. 3.3)

fitted_gratings.note: G fitted to MAN Table 6 A/px with sourced optics (T06); all inside T06's 200-500 /mm and 30-47 deg
